listings.name: People's Committee Hall
listings.content: Built as the Hôtel de Ville, it's a striking cream and yellow French colonial building beautifully floodlit at night. No entry, but the statue of Uncle Ho in front is a very popular place for photos.

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh Museum
listings.content: The museum, housed in a French colonial-era building, narrates the history of Ho Chi Minh City from pre-history to the present and also has exhibits on local culture and traditions. Outside, on the museum grounds, you will find cars and military vehicles of historical significance. The museum also relates the life of the modern-day father of Vietnam. The exhibits include various personal possessions of Ho Chi Minh but are mainly photographs. You may find it a little jingoistic.
listings.image: Bảo tàng Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh 7.jpg

listings.name: Museum of Vietnamese History
listings.content: The museum has a fine collection of Vietnamese antiquities. Read up on Vietnamese history first or you'll have no idea what you're looking at. Outside, the Botanical Gardens are very nice and a good place for a cheap lunch away from the crowds. Six times a day, you can see a 20-minute water puppet show (adult 50,000 dong, child 35,000 dong). It's quite amusing, even for adults.
listings.address: 2 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1

listings.name: Independence Palace
listings.content: This is a restored 4-floor time warp to the 1960s left largely untouched from the day Saigon fell to the North; construction started in 1962 and finished in 1966. It was South Vietnam's presidential palace. The war ended on 30 Apr 1975 when Tank 843 crashed through the gate. A replica of that tank is now parked on the lawn outside. Be sure to check out the aggressively 1960s recreation room on the third floor, featuring a circular sofa, and the eerie basement, full of vintage 1960s phones, radios and office equipment, supposedly left exactly as it was found when the North took over. There is also a photo gallery and a propaganda film recounting how the South Vietnamese supporters and American imperialists succumbed to Ho Chi Minh's indomitable revolutionary forces, at which point the South Vietnamese supporters were forgiven and everyone lived happily ever after. Free guided tours and an audio guide are available (90,000 dong). The audio guide is extremely informative, but not necessary. There is a nice outdoor café on the grounds outside the palace.

listings.name: War Remnants Museum
listings.content: The museum was opened in a hurry, less than five months after the fall of the South Vietnamese regime. It has moved to new premises with 3 storeys of exhibits and various US military hardware (tanks, jets, helicopters, howitzers) on display outside the building. This disturbing display of man's cruelty during the Vietnam (American) War includes halls full of gruesome photographs, a simulated "tiger cage" prison and jars of deformed foetuses attributed to contamination by Agent Orange. An exhibit on the 3rd floor tells the story of the war journalists from all over the world who documented, and often disappeared or died in the war. Watch out for the amputees who will try to sell you their wares on the museum grounds, though largely their wares take the form of only somewhat overpriced books on historical topics relevant to the museum, and are less of a scam than more of an informal gift shop. The museum is a short walk from Reunification Palace — see the museum pamphlet for a map.

listings.name: Southern Women’s Museum
listings.content: Often overlooked by tourists, this museum celebrates the women’s role in the society, economy, and revolutionary history of the southern part of the country. It offers informative exhibits that include photographs, historical documents, and artifacts such as statues, combat equipment used by women, paintings and dioramas, tools used in the traditional production of textiles, and ao dai worn by famous women. As of a February 2018, the second floor had an exhibit on the history of the ao dai and another on textile production, the third floor detailed women’s revolutionary contributions, and the fourth floor was under renovation.

listings.name: FITO Museum of Traditional Vietnamese Medicine
listings.content: A small museum owned by the FITO company (they produce traditional pharmaceuticals) about the history of traditional medicine in Vietnam. The rooms are filled with items ranging from ingredients to tools used to produce and prepare Vietnamese medicine. Each ticket includes an informative tour of the museum and the opportunity to sample some products. The bottom floor also has a gift shop with competitively priced and high-quality traditional remedies.

listings.name: The Geological Museum of Vietnam
listings.content: A rare gem and a must see for geology & natural history enthusiasts. This 3-story building houses a collection of earthly artifacts (and even some non-earthly ones), including a few rare examples. Sadly in a state of neglect with poor lighting and little to no interpretive text. You can read more about it here.
listings.address: 2 Đ. Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
listings.content: Museum displaying art mainly from the 20th century by Vietnamese artists. Two floors of permanent collections are in the main building and the first floor of the second building has a special exhibitions space. The architecture of the French colonial buildings that house the museum is another impressive feature. They were designed by a French architect for the Hua family.
listings.address: 97A Phó Đức Chính, Phường Nguyễn Thái Bìn, District 1

listings.name: Saigon Opera House
listings.content: An opera house built by the French during the colonial period, and without a doubt one of the finest performance venues in Southeast Asia. In modern times it is home to the critically acclaimed AO show, an acrobatic show that fuses Vietnamese traditions with modern Cirque Nouveau performances. Occasionally hosts classical music performances when the AO show is not being performed.
listings.address: 7 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City

listings.name: Ton Duc Thang Museum
listings.content: A museum detailing the life and achievements of politician Ton Duc Thang, known for his role as president. The first floor has a special exhibit (as of February 2018 about his time on the infamous prison island of Con Dao) and the second floor has a biographical display featuring artifacts, dioramas, and photographs telling the story of his life; there is also a painting gallery.
listings.address: 5 Tôn Đức Thắng, Bến Nghé, District 1

listings.name: The Venerable Thich Quảng Đức Monument
listings.content: A monument dedicated to the Buddhist monk Thich Quảng Đức, who self-immolated at the site in 1963 in protest against the persecution of South Vietnam's Buddhist majority by the Roman Catholic-dominated Ngô Đình Diệm government.
listings.address: intersection between Cach Mang Thang Tam & Nguyen Dinh Chieu streets

listings.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
listings.content: A Taoist temple considered by many to be Saigon’s finest, dedicated to the Jade Emperor, the king of the gods in Chinese mythology. Built by Cantonese immigrants in 1909. Check out the room filled with unusual figurines, to the left of the main hall. There are many turtles in a concrete pond in the courtyard. A calm place to rest from the city noise.

listings.name: Xá Lợi Pagoda
listings.content: The largest Buddhist temple in Ho Chi Minh City, and the headquarters of Buddhism in South Vietnam prior to the Fall of Saigon, said to house relics of the Gautama Buddha. During the Vietnam War, it was known for being a centre of resistance against the oppression of Buddhists by the Roman Catholic-dominated Ngô Đình Diệm government, and was raided several times by the South Vietnamese military in 1963.
listings.address: 89 Bà Huyện Thanh Quan, Võ Thị Sáu, Quận 3

listings.name: Giác Lâm Pagoda
listings.content: Built in 1744, this is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Ho Chi Minh City. On the temple grounds is a bodhi tree that was gifted by a Sri Lankan monk in the 1950s. There is also a 7-storey tall pagoda that is said to house relics of the Gautama Buddha that were gifted by the same monk that gifted the bodhi tree.
listings.address: 565 Lạc Long Quân, Phường 10, Tân Bình

listings.name: Central Mosque
listings.content: One of 12 mosques in Ho Chi Minh City, the Central Mosque was built in 1935. It was constructed for worshipers from southern India then resident in Saigon, but now Muslims from as far as Pakistan and Indonesia come to pray. Friday has the biggest congregations. The shaded veranda and cool stone floors make it an ideal place to sit, read, or even nap in the heat of the day. As with most mosques, remember to take your shoes off before entering and dress conservatively if you wish to enter.

listings.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
listings.content: A French-built Catholic cathedral in the city center.

listings.name: Mariamman Temple
listings.content: Hindu temple build by Tamil Indian immigrants in the late 19th century. Although most of the Tamils fled Vietnam following the Fall of Saigon, the temple remains in active use, and today most of the devotees are ethnic Vietnamese or Khmers.
listings.address: 45 Trương Định, Phường Bến Thành, Quận 1

listings.name: Phung Son Tu Pagoda
listings.content: Dedicated to the god of happiness and virtue. The pagoda is dusty and dwarfed by high-rises under construction nearby, but the small, sculpted grounds are a good place for a rest from the hectic city.

listings.name: Quan Am Pagoda
listings.content: The oldest pagoda in town, dedicated to the Buddhist Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara (known as Quan Am in Vietnamese), home of a lot of incense and a cheerful puppy. It was built by Hokkien immigrants in the traditional Hokkien architectural style.
listings.image: Quan Âm Pagoda - Front entrance edited.jpg

listings.name: Thien Hau Pagoda
listings.content: Dedicated to Lady Thien Hau, the Chinese sea goddess (known as Mazu in Chinese), who left two giant turtles to keep an eye on things in her absence. A festival is held in her honour on the 23rd day of the March lunar month. Don't miss the gorgeous sculptures in the walls of the courtyard outside the temple. It was built by Cantonese immigrants in the traditional Cantonese architectural style.

listings.name: Bitexco Financial Tower
listings.content: Skydeck viewing platform (daily 09:30-21:30) with a 360° panorama of the city.
listings.price: Adult 240k VND, child (4-12) / senior (65+) / disabled 160k VND

listings.name: IMAX cinema
listings.content: Vietnam's IMAX cinema.

listings.name: Landmark 81
listings.content: The highest tower of Vietnam with 81 floors which is 461.3 m, it has a big mall inside which includes a CGV cinema. Landmark 81 are also surrounded in a complex of apartments as part of Vinhomes' Tan Cang, or Central Park. Access the views by paying for SkyView (top 3 floors; 300k/500k weekdays/weekends, children/elderly half price; 200k for VND students on weekdays) or by patronizing one of the restaurants/cafes/lounges on the upper floors (prices vary, but tend to be 100k+ VND, high for Vietnam but about average for global HCOL cities; these are accessible through the Marriott Autograph Collection hotel by transferring elevators at the hotel's skylobby). There's also reasonably priced local and international food in the food court on the lower level.
listings.price: No entry fees but has parking fees for vehicles

listings.name: Dai Nam Tourist Park
listings.content: This is one of the largest tourist attractions in Vietnam. It features the Dai Nam Van Hien Temple, an entertainment site, open range zoo, shopping areas, hotels, local and Western cuisine, and the largest man-made mountain range in Vietnam. Costing over 50 billion dong to build, this park is the beginning of mass tourism in Vietnam, although it is aimed at tourists and locals, and comes highly recommended. Transport options to the park are quite convoluted. As the park is new, online information is scarce. According to the locals, it is very much worth a visit, purely just to view the temple.
listings.price: Adult/child between 1 m and 1.4 m: zoo 80,000/50,000; amusement park 100,000/50,000 dong; waterpark 100,000/60,000 dong; all three 200,000/120,000 dong
listings.address: Hiệp An Ward, Thủ Dầu Một city, Binh Duong

listings.name: Dam Sen Water Park
listings.content: Close to the city centre. This water park offers some unique water slide experiences, including the amazing "Space Bowl". Restaurant, health services and animatronic dinosaurs are on the premises.
listings.price: Admission is based on height and time of arrival; under 0.8 m free, others 40-110,000 dong (90,000 after 16:00)

listings.name: Happy Ending Massage Yuan
listings.content: Despite the name, legitimate foot and body massage, hostess will explain pricing to you at the beginning, usually offering 30% discount.
listings.address: 15B8 Le Thanh Ton St, District 1 Ben Nighe Ward

listings.name: Twenty-Three September Park
listings.content: Running along Phan Ngu Lao St are a number of parks which fill up with locals before sunset, after work. They play a variety of games which you can participate in: badminton, kicking a shuttlecock and women's group aerobics to music are all very popular, and are great to watch. If you sit down by yourself in the open area near the Ben Thanh market a number of young university age locals will come and ask to practice English with you, this is a great way to spend an evening and the best way to meet intelligent interesting youth, they will question you either individually or in groups and share with you a lot about their country. Beware of those men who want to introduce you to their "sister" who's working as a nurse and wants to move to your country. They will try to make you come into their home so you can reassure their parents, but will actually gamble and cheat at cards with you and/or ask you for money after telling a sad and fake story about some dying relative.

listings.name: Nguyen Hue Flower Street
listings.content: Beautiful assortment of flowers during Tet (Lunar New Year) along the popular boulevard in District 1.

listings.name: Vietnamese Language Garden
listings.content: The school offers one-on-one study,focus on intensive classes to get fluent in Vietnamese in a short time, or 1-2 weeks classes for tourist & homes stay to experience the local lifestyle
listings.address: 135/10 Nguyen Cuu Van, Binh Thanh District

listings.name: Vietnamese Language Studies
listings.content: Private school with comprehensive courses from beginner to advanced composition. Students can take private courses or join group classes.

listings.name: VNS University
listings.content: In District 1, the University of Social Sciences has comprehensive university-style courses in Vietnamese, group classes typically 6-10 people.

listings.name: Ben Thanh Market
listings.content: It's a rather touristy market where you still can enjoy the most authentic Vietnamese pho.

listings.name: Bánh Mì 37
listings.content: Absolutely delicious even though a bit different than the traditional. Popular among locals, there might be a queue.

listings.name: Pho 24
listings.content: Clean modern chain found everywhere in Ho Chi Minh City. Excellent beef noodle soup, very cheap. Watch out for the fake Pho 24/24 on Pham Ngu Lao St, which does not belong to the chain and serves terrible and expensive food.

listings.name: Pho Quynh
listings.content: Their specialty is pho. Locals come regularly and lucky backpackers stumble upon it. It is air-conditioned on the second and third floors. They also have decent banh mi bo kho, which is beef stew with carrots, served with French baguette.

listings.name: Nhà Hàng Chay Ngọc Thọ
listings.content: Incredible range of delicoius veggie options, but also meat and chicken. Clean place, friendly staff, tasty food and satisfying portions.

listings.name: Nhà Hàng Asian Kitchen
listings.content: Very good place for delicious and diverse food, big choice. Kinda hidden, kinda great. Also lots of vegetarian options.

listings.name: Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa
listings.content: Banh Mi with local taste. Fresh bread (Vietnamese baguette) with various choices.

listings.name: Bún Chả 145
listings.content: Typical restaurant in the most amazing street of the city. Very good place for Bun Cha. As of February 2026, it is closed for renovation.

listings.name: The Lunch Lady
listings.content: The famous Lunch Lady was featured on Anthony Bourdain's show. Different noodle dish every day.

listings.name: Barbecue Garden
listings.content: A barbecue restaurant offering both Vietnamese and international foods.

listings.name: Bi Saigon
listings.content: Extensive menu with a choice between Vietnamese, Italian, Mexican and other styles. Open plan kitchen so you can see your food being prepared.

listings.name: Hoa Khai Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.content: Tasty Vietnamese vegetarian food although with surly service. Be careful of being charged for unexpected items, such as the disposable hand towels that are presented to you without asking as you sit down.
listings.address: 124 126 Nguyen Cu Trinh St, Cu Trinh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát
listings.content: Restaurant selling Hủ tiếu Nam Vang, a flat rice noodle dish that is a specialty of the city. The dish is often called "Cambodian noodles" in English, even though it cannot be found in Cambodia.

listings.name: Quan An Ngon
listings.content: Two different restaurants operate with the same name within a few blocks of each other, one at 160 Pasteur Street, and the other type=eat name=Quán ăn ngon Sài Gòn lat 10.7776569 long = 106.6975984 on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia across from the Reunification Palace. Set in atmospheric old French villas, with similar menus Vietnamese food, including regional specialities prepared in numerous independently-operated food stalls around the perimeter. Both are popular and both tend to be jammed at peak hours requiring a wait for a table. (The name literally means "restaurant of delicious eating".) The one on Pasteur has dozens of kerosene lamps burning for ambience at night, so if you have asthma or pulmonary issues or feel you've had enough pollution already, better to try the other one.

listings.name: Bloom Saigon Restaurant
listings.content: Temporarily closed as of August 2022. Non-profit restaurant run by Aid to Children Without Parents (ACWP) and serves as a culinary training facility. Very nice staff, excellent food, terrace on the 3rd floor. Situated a bit in the North and in a small calm community. Worth to go by foot, 20 mnin walk from the Jade Pagoda.
listings.address: 3/5 Hoàng Sa, P. Đa Kao, Quận 1

listings.name: Au Lac do Brazil
listings.content: Just to prove that Saigon has everything, here is a Brazilian-style churrascaria (all-you-can-eat restaurant featuring barbecued meat), with live Latin music Tuesday to Saturday. They also have a new outlet in Sky Garden II, Phu My Hung, District 7. It's a larger and less crowded one with usually better service.

listings.name: The Deck Saigon
listings.content: The only posh restaurant on the banks of the river. Modern fusion cuisine using the local ingredients.
listings.address: 38 Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien, An Phu, District 2

listings.name: Anan Saigon
listings.content: A premier fine dining restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, one of only two in Vietnam to be ranked among Asia's top 50 restaurants. Reservations essential.
listings.address: 89 Tôn Thất Đạm, Bến Nghé, District 1

listings.name: The Olive Grove Saigon
listings.content: Mediterranean cuisine.

listings.name: Halal@Saigon
listings.content: Vietnamese, Malaysian, and vegetarian cuisine prepared to halal guidelines. Has a Malaysian owner and there are several Malaysian staples on the menu, however it is primarily Vietnamese, with a wide range of dishes from around the country.

listings.name: Lion City Cafe and Restaurant
listings.content: Certified halal, serves halal food on 2nd floor.

listings.name: Bobby Brewery Coffee
listings.content: Nice place with good beverages. Used to show movies on 2nd and 3rd floor. Now reopened as La Cantina.

listings.name: Cafe 5 Sao
listings.content: Plays loud techno music. Attractive, but pretentious crowd.

listings.name: Cafe Napoly
listings.content: The decor is Roman ruins-lite (they meant "Napoli"), but the menu is typical for an upscale Vietnamese cafe: coffee, fruit drinks, ice cream, and a simple menu including eggs and rice dishes. Piped music is nice, not too loud by day (though louder at night), prices are decent. Outdoor terrace in the front, air-con section on the ground floor, and evening lounge-bar on the upper floor. Next door to the louder, more trendy and possibly pretentious Cafe Nam Sao.

listings.name: Cafe Saigon
listings.content: Italian coffee, foods, free Wi-Fi, relaxing & modern music.

listings.name: Chao Ba Ca Phe
listings.content: This place has a really authentic and wonderful cafe sua da served by the famous "grandma" for about 8,000 dong. A little tricky to find.

listings.name: Chot Nho Café
listings.content: Reasonable prices, good menu. Free Wi-Fi.
listings.address: 189 Nguyen Van Troi, Phu Nhuan District

listings.name: Fresco Coffee
listings.content: Free Wi-Fi, play hill song music.

listings.name: Givral Café
listings.content: In the French tradition, with fresh pastries, collared waiters and elaborate portions of ice cream. Well-located, but over 20,000 dong for the simplest cup.

listings.name: Hideaway Café
listings.content: As its name implies, this place is hidden away and a good place to read, or have a quiet conversation or meal. Decent Western menu, although slightly pricey.

listings.name: Highlands Coffee
listings.content: Highlands Coffee is a Vietnamese chain that is ubiquitous in Ho Chi Minh City. They offer a variety of coffee drinks reasonably priced (25,000-60,000 dong, depending on your order) with consistent quality.

listings.name: M-Comic
listings.content: A rather hard to find coffee shop. Upstairs is like a bedroom with a couple of beds. Arrive early if you want to occupy one. It has a large selection of magazine and comic books to choose from. Only serves Vietnamese drinks, and the staff only speak a little English. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Old Saigon Coffee
listings.content: Reminiscent of HCMC in the past. It has a great view of Dong Khoi St. All the drinks and foods are typical Saigon. The staff are quite decent.

listings.name: Regina Coffee
listings.content: Vietnamese coffee or cappuccini. They have a skilled Japanese espresso master who knows how to brew coffee. French mixed with Asian design with brick walls. It is marketed towards tourists and all proceeds go to the church around the corner.

listings.name: Trung Nguyen
listings.content: The Vietnamese version of Starbucks, but with much better coffee. They have locations all over the city, but are not well represented in the heart of the tourist district. Prices start around 40,000 dong for a basic cuppa, although there are plenty of variations including the infamous weasel coffee (cà phê chồn), made from coffee beans collected from civet excrement; however, a quick Google search about the conditions in which the civets are kept may further dissuade some from sampling.

listings.name: Chill Sky Bar
listings.content: Rooftop bar at AB Tower in District 1 along September 23 park. This is the place to see and to be seen. Drinks are expensive at 200,000 dong and up. If you are around the September 23 park at night you will see the lights and hear the music blasting from the top of the AB tower. Look for the spotlights shooting into the sky.

listings.name: The Rabbit Hole Irish Sports Bar
listings.content: Irish Sports bar.
listings.address: 111 Pham Viet Chanh, Ward 19, Binh Thanh

listings.name: Acoustic Cafe
listings.content: Though only 1 km from the heavily touristed centre, this club is completely outside the tourist orbit, and offers an interesting view of local life. The all-Vietnamese house band performs every night, mostly American music, and it's always jammed with student-aged groupies. For some reason, they address the crowd in English between songs, even though half the crowd doesn't understand. On weekends, at least, you need to arrive by 19:30 to have any hope of getting a seat. If your hobby is rock ballad or hard rock, you should go on Friday night.

listings.name: Banana Pub
listings.content: Park View. Pool table, darts, friendly staff, beautiful people, loads of food. Stays open late depending on the crowd. Worth a trip from Q1 to experience the expat scene.

listings.name: Carmen
listings.content: The house band has changed some personnel but is still good, specializing in flamenco, salsa and Latin pop, and with an eclectic mix of other popular songs thrown in. Cocktails 110,000 dong, shots 80-85,000 dong, but with no entrance charge. It's popular and fills up on weekends.

listings.name: Ice Blue
listings.content: Centrally located English pub, complete with darts board and warm beer. Friendly, but shuts at midnight.

listings.name: Khong Ten
listings.content: Large cabaret featuring some of the biggest Vietnamese celebrity singers in Vietnam. The headliner is often familiar to the locals from television. Most overseas visitors may not like the musical style as it is mostly the mellow-to-melancholy, soft-jazzy, love-ballady style favoured by the middle and older generation of Vietnamese. But it's pure Vietnam, and very popular with both HCMC residents and Vietnamese expats on trips home.

listings.name: Lion's
listings.content: Brewery, restaurant offering German food, with tasty beers and cocktails. The outside terrace is a nice place to chill out, and the inside restaurant is very welcoming with its two beer tanks and cosy bar.

listings.name: Lush
listings.content: A nightclub in the Western style, with loud music and minimalist too-cool decor. Drink prices on par with most Saigon nightclubs. Mixed crowd (Vietnamese, tourists and expats), pretty good food but has a small dance floor. Ladies night on Tuesday offers free drinks for ladies until midnight. Be sure to arrive early as it gets very busy from around 22:30 and it is difficult to get served at the bar.

listings.name: Metallic Bar
listings.content: House band plays covers of Metallica, Guns 'n Roses and other popular rock bands nightly between 21:00 and midnight.

listings.name: Peaches
listings.content: Great place to enjoy a few drinks with friends. Friendly staff, Asian food. Quite low key in comparison to other PMH bars.

listings.name: Polo
listings.content: Mixture of expats and locals, starts getting busy quite early. Music from the 1980s to the present. Noisy and smokey.

listings.name: Q Bar Saigon
listings.content: Established in 1992 under the Opera House. Mix of locals, tourists and expats in a grotto-like uber-chic setting that could as easily be in Soho as Saigon. Open till late every night. Great cocktails, though at very high prices, similar to the roof-top bar of the Caravelle Hotel across the street. It's the cool place to be seen if you have a lot of Uncle Hos in your pocket. Terrace and Indoor areas. DJ nights.

listings.name: Rio Saigon
listings.content: A Brazilian flowery decor-themed bar/pub with a Filipino house band playing pop/rock such as Bon Jovi and Skid Row.

listings.name: Saigon Pho
listings.content: This little hole in the wall is only a stone's throw from Allez Boo, but much more expat orientated. Open until late.

listings.name: Serenata and Soi Da
listings.content: Two open-air cafe-bars with live music in villa-style settings, which attract few if any tourists but typify what most Vietnamese consider a pleasant evening out. Both feature a mix of classical chamber music, Vietnamese lounge songs, American FM classics and the odd French song.

listings.name: The Tavern
listings.content: Western food with fish & chips and burgers.
listings.address: SB8-1 My Khanh 2 (H4-2) Nguyen Van Linh, Phu My Hung District

listings.name: Velvet
listings.content: Nice ambiance & music. Latest chic bar in town. Gets very busy, and at weekends you will need a booking.

listings.name: Xu Bar
listings.content: Great wine list. Nice ambiance & service.

listings.name: Alibi
listings.content: Very cosy atmosphere, with sofas lining the walls and beautiful decor. Good food & drinks selection, nice music, and a mix of both locals & expats. Friendly staff, and the management's always there to make you feel welcome and make sure you get what you are asking for.

listings.name: Allez Boo
listings.content: For those who have been here before, you'll find the original bar is now Highlands Coffee and an all new Allez Boo has opened on the opposite corner. It's shiny and brand-new, but retains the same feel as the original. There's a bar with air-con on the 2nd floor with DJ-type music, and an airy rooftop patio. Quite similar to its sibling establishment, Go2 Bar.

listings.name: Apocalypse Now
listings.content: Legendary and still packed on weekends, although aside from a few movie references it's not all that much to look at. Stays open late. Now opened their 2nd floor for DJ, dancing, drinks with less crowded atmosphere.

listings.name: Catwalk
listings.content: All-in-one place with a massage parlour, disco, KTV, and a mini-casino. Price is on the expensive side, but it is a sight to behold.

listings.name: Go2 Bar
listings.content: The main backpacker bar while Allez Boo was closed, still a great meeting place. It's impossible to miss the four floors of neon lights on the outside. Large patio on the sidewalk at street level, a cosier bar on the second floor with occasional live music or big-screen sports, plus a rooftop patio (with retractable roof) with individual BBQs up a steep set of stairs on the 5th floor.

listings.name: Oblivion
listings.content: Late night venue with lots of character, claims to be Saigon's premier music bar and it's hard to argue, assuming, that is, you have a taste for non-chart buzzy British guitar and obscure dark US/European stuff. You have to ask for happy pop, though if you're spending enough it'll sometimes get an outing. Like most Saigon bars, it attracts its share of working girls. If you're not interested, simply say you're not and you'll be left alone.

listings.name: Pasteur Street Brewing Company
listings.content: A cozy bar that specializes in craft beer microbrews. A large selection of their own beers that run between 50,000-300,000 dong per glass (though most are 105,000 for a regular size). They also serve food and bar snacks. Mostly expats and tourists with a laid back yet classy atmosphere. The original tap rooms are down an alley off Pasteur Street, but there are clearly marked signs to guide you from the street.
listings.address: 144 Pasteur, Bến Nghé, District 1 (this is the original location, but others can be found throughout the city)

listings.name: 163 Cyclo Bar
listings.content: Two doors down from the Duna Hotel. Thumping music until 02:00 with friendly staff. Sex workers catering to Western men here. If you're not interested, just gently let it be known.

listings.name: Le Pub
listings.content: Always busy after 18:00, famous for its strong drinks, daily dollar-specials (e.g., Tuesday USD1 for vodka mixers all night) and friendly staff. It has the same owner as Le Pub in Hanoi. The Pub Quiz (almost every Tuesday) is very popular with expats, especially the English teachers. Get there early or it's too packed to find a place to sit down. Indoors and outdoor tables available.

listings.name: Rex Hotel Rooftop
listings.content: They serve a buffet dinner at the dinner hour, which gradually gives way to drinks and music. Acts change over time, but have included a Filipino band playing FM classics and a Vietnamese group playing Latin and flamenco. It's a pleasant place to get above the city noise and enjoy some fresh air. Cocktails around 140,000 dong.

listings.name: Saigon Saigon
listings.content: A pleasant, breezy bar with a great view of the city. Great live band (Cuban) playing inside every night. Cool, quiet ambience on the terrace. Attracts an expense-account crowd due to the prices.

listings.name: Seventeen Saloon
listings.content: American Wild West-themed bar, live music every night and other entertainment. Drinks are expensive.

listings.name: Sheridan's
listings.content: Small, cosy Irish-themed bar with imported draft beer and live music. Brits will appreciate the great food tasting of home (or the closest you'll get here).

listings.name: Vasco's
listings.content: Live music on some nights of the week and a typical bar atmosphere for tourists and expats. Drinks from 50,000 dong, including sales tax, tip not necessary.

listings.name: VIBE Billiards & Lounge
listings.content: Professional billiards tables and a spacious lounge. Food and drinks and you can customise the billiard table lights from a special lighting system.
listings.address: 02 Sương Nguyệt Ánh, Phường Bến Thành, Quận 1

listings.name: ZanZBar
listings.content: Casual-upscale, the clients tend to come for the great choice of wines-by-the-glass (huge walk-in wine cellar), or for the cocktails (premium brands) and good selection of imported beers. Can remain open after midnight, depending on the number of customers.

listings.name: An Phuong 2
listings.content: A friendly family-run guesthouse, very clean and homely. Free Internet, cheap laundry and all rooms have double glazing.

listings.name: Blue River Hotel
listings.content: Amazing small hotel in an alley off Pham Ngu Lao. They can arrange an airport pickup for USD15, although an official taxi from the airport counter will cost USD8. Some staff members speak English and the service is good.
listings.price: USD25 for a room without a view. USD30 for a room with a view that may or may not have a balcony

listings.name: Dai Huy Hoang Hotel
listings.content: Comfortable rooms with air-con, fan, free Internet and breakfast. Friendly staff.

listings.name: Diep Anh
listings.content: Very friendly owners. Rooms with air-con, refrigerator, cable TV, en suite bath, and Wi-Fi. Very reasonably priced minibar.

listings.name: Duna Hotel
listings.content: All rooms have air-con, satellite TV, a fridge, elevator. Pleasant staff. The front door is locked around 23:00-24:00.
listings.price: From USD12 for a single room with no window to USD30 for a triple with a window facing the street.

listings.name: Hanh Hoa Hotel
listings.content: Vietnamese styling, with bamboo interiors, rattan beds and wooden floors.

listings.name: Hotel Bi Saigon
listings.content: Clean, comfortable, and terrific staff. In-room Internet access for USD3/day. The lobby houses the La Table de Saigon restaurant.

listings.name: Ly
listings.content: Family-run guest house with friendly staff who speak English. Air-con, hot water, cable TV with international channels, baggage storage, laundry service, big beds. with balconies.

listings.name: Ly Loan
listings.content: Family-run guest house in a small, safe, quiet alley. Some English is spoken. Rooms are spacious and nicely furnished. With air-con, hot water, big beds and some with balconies. Free Internet and Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Mai Guest House
listings.content: Friendly family. Tucked in a side alley from Pham Ngu Lao or Bui Viên next to My Home Guest Home. Small balcony. Clean apartments with aircon and Wi-Fi. 15,000 or 30,000 dong per kg for 24 hr or express laundry.
listings.price: Doubles USD12, doubles with balcony USD15
listings.address: Hem 104 Bui Viên or 241 /41 Phạm Ngũ Lão, District 1

listings.name: My Home Guest House
listings.content: Friendly staff and clean. The buses from up north drop you right near this hostel. Air-con, hot water, comfortable beds, free Wi-Fi. Free bananas at all times and they do laundry. Tourist bars and clubs are a couple hundred metres away.
listings.price: Singles USD12, doubles USD18, triples available

listings.name: Nam Chau
listings.content: Nice and very clean.

listings.name: Galaxy Boutique Hotel
listings.address: 269/19 De Tham Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1

listings.name: Ngoc Minh Hotel
listings.content: Clean hotel with friendly staff, free Internet and Wi-Fi. Elevator. 5 storeys, garden on top floor and free breakfast.

listings.name: Nguyen Khang Hotel
listings.content: Good staff, free Internet with PC in lobby and Wi-Fi in rooms. Free breakfast served on the ground floor from 07:00-10:00. Clean, tastefully simple in decoration, rooms are rather small but have air-con, fan, TV, fridge, and those at the front have large windows. Visa and Mastercard accepted.

listings.name: PP Backpackers
listings.content: Run by a friendly Englishman, offers clean dorms and rooms, can book tours and offers a big breakfast for USD1.

listings.name: Rainbow Hotel
listings.content: Large, bright albeit somewhat worn rooms, and those at the front have a nice view.

listings.name: Tam Anh Guesthouse
listings.content: A clean and secure family-run guesthouse. Good air-con, free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Tan Dat My Hotel
listings.content: Large rooms with a view, air-con, Wi-Fi, fridge, cable TV and a free rooftop breakfast next to the Dam Sen Park. French bakery 30 m away. American-style supermarket 10 min walk on the same street.

listings.name: Thanh Guest House
listings.content: Warm and friendly guesthouse. Lobby inside the house with comfy sofa, cable TV and Internet. Free Wi-Fi throughout. Trips and tours can be booked at reception.
listings.address: 84/9 Bui Vien, Pham Ngu Lao, District 1

listings.name: Thien Hong Hotel
listings.content: Helpful and friendly owners, free Wi-Fi, TV in rooms with many channels including international.
listings.price: Air-con room with no window, USD15

listings.name: Ty Mon
listings.content: Friendly owners, very good basic rooms with air-con, TV, decent furniture and fridge. Very cheap price, mostly used by Vietnamese people. A bit far out from centre.

listings.name: Xuan Spring Hotel
listings.content: Air-con, refrigerator, cable TV and private bath with hot shower and free Internet. Online bookings. Good service.

listings.name: Mi Linh Hotel
listings.content: a/c standard double room with own bathroom and cable tv. Free Wifi. a good clean place to stay near the HCM Airport.
listings.address: B38A Bach Dang Street Ward 02 Tan Binh District.

listings.name: Lee Hostel Home For Backpackers
listings.content: 20 bed dorm with air.con and hot water free wifi. free breakfast. Some complaints that they will insist on holding your passport hostage even after you've paid, various other scammy practices.

listings.name: Bich Hong Guest House
listings.content: Fan and a/c double rooms with own bathroom.

listings.name: Kim Loan Guest House
listings.content: Fan double with own bathroom.

listings.name: 4 Guest House Thanh
listings.content: Fan double room with own bathroom.

listings.name: Christina's Saigon
listings.content: A flashpacker guesthouse and bed & breakfast. The studios are beautifully designed with modern bathrooms. Booking is only available through Airbnb.
listings.address: 212/2B Nguyen Trai St., Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Asian Hotel
listings.content: Every room has air-con, cable TV, and Internet.
listings.address: 146-148-150 Dong Khoi St, Ben Nghe District

listings.name: Platinum Boutique Residence and Hotel
listings.content: Lovely modern, clean hotel. Rooms come with double-glazed windows, LCD flat screen TVs, and wall-mounted air conditioning controls. The suite has a spa bath. Free Wi-Fi and friendly staff.
listings.address: 270 Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Dai Nam Hotel
listings.content: Breakfast and free in-room Wi-Fi. Houses the Gossip Nightclub.

listings.name: Asian Ruby Select Hotel
listings.content: All rooms and suites have air-con, TV with satellite channels, IDD telephone, coffee/tea maker and minibar. Bar, cafe, spa and massage services, business centre, gym and high speed Internet access. Annoyingly, housekeeping have a tendency to knock on bedroom doors early in the morning, but then don't make up the rooms until early afternoon.
listings.address: 122F-122F1 Bui Thi Xuan, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1

listings.name: Ngoc Ha
listings.content: Clean, decent rooms, air-con, fridge, Wi-Fi in the lobby.

listings.name: Nhat Ha Hotel
listings.content: 57 rooms decorated with traditional Vietnamese handicrafts. IDD telephone, satellite TV, mini-bar, and air-con.
listings.address: 252 BC Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Sanouva Hotel
listings.content: Air-con, 32" LCD TV with cable, Internet, and IDD telephone. Restaurant, bar, café, car rental, travel bookings, tour services and safes.
listings.address: 175-177 Ly Tu Trong St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Spring Hotel
listings.content: Clean, boutique hotel that is walking distance to major attractions such as Ben Thanh Market and the cathedral.

listings.name: Thuan Thien Hotel
listings.content: Air-con rooms, cable TV, DVD, coffee/tea maker, minibar and a private toilet and shower with bath. Internet, dry cleaning, and laundry service and a travel agency for booking tours.
listings.address: 277 Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1

listings.name: Y Thien
listings.content: Full service hotel with a range of clean rooms with large baths. Sizes from tiny and windowless (yet functional), to full wall window overlooking the city and streets. The 4th floor room to the right of the elevator is USD20–25. Cable TV, air-con, fan, refrigerator, elevator, all night guard for bikes, hotel safe. A good option if you don't want to stay in the backpacker area and are willing to pay a little more.

listings.name: Somerset Vista Ho Chi Minh City
listings.content: The property has apartments ranging from two- to four-bedroom with kitchenette, washing machines and dryers. They have an on-site tennis court.
listings.address: No. 628C Hanoi Highway, An Phu, District 2

listings.name: An An Hotel
listings.content: Clean, popular, and offers comfortable rooms with double glazing in the centre of the action on De Tham. Free Wi-Fi in room and lobby.

listings.name: An An 2 Hotel
listings.content: This is the (much newer) sister hotel to An An hotel.
listings.price: From USD22 (with window) for standard single, USD25 for double and USD36–50 for superior and luxury with balcony. The prices can be lowered if you stay for 4 or more days (e.g., USD20 for double for 6 days)

listings.name: Continental Hotel
listings.content: An old-school colonial hotel dating back to 1880 and the setting of Graham Greene's novel The Quiet American. Beautiful garden courtyard, huge rooms, nice balcony views. On the minus side, there is no pool and traffic noise can be irritating,.

listings.name: Hotel Đông Đô
listings.content: New hotel with clean and comfortable rooms.

listings.name: The First Hotel
listings.content: Luxury hotel, 104 air-con rooms, cable TV, mini-bar, shower with bath, and Wi-Fi. Casino and ballroom, fitness room, tennis court, swimming pool, airport transfer, and car rental.
listings.address: 18 Hoang Viet St, Ward 4, Tan Binh District

listings.name: Ho Sen Hotel
listings.content: Clean and comfortable rooms with air-con and bar fridge. Right around the corner is the Apocalypse Now Club. Breakfast included, free Wi-Fi in the lobby, while connections are a little patchy in the rooms.
listings.address: 4A-4B Thi Sach St, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1

listings.name: Mekong Lodge
listings.content: A good hotel for those who love nature.
listings.address: 196/1/20 Cong Hoa St, Tan Binh District

listings.name: Rex Hotel
listings.content: Another old standby, former haunt of the press corps and site of the daily "Five O'Clock Follies" news briefing during the Vietnam War. The 5th floor rooftop beer garden is famous and its symbol, the golden crown, is rotating again. The rooms are very pleasant and there is a swimming pool on the roof. Buffet breakfast.

listings.name: Thien Thao Hotel
listings.content: A small hotel with thin walls but also clean and comfortable with air-con rooms, bathtubs, local and cable channels on a large plasma TV, and minibar fridge. About 20 min walk away from the heart of District 1. Bakery and several restaurants less than 5 min away, free Wi-Fi in the rooms and three computers in the lobby.

listings.name: Xuan Loc Hotel
listings.content: Clean and comfortable rooms. Breakfast available. Internet and computers are provided.

listings.name: M Village
listings.content: A chain with a number of furnished short/long-term stay apartment rentals scattered throughout the city (both in and outside of touristy areas) that supports hotel-like bookings (as little as 1 night, no extra charges). Typically includes free self-service, first come first serve laundry machines and a small in-room kitchenette. English is a bit spotty, but serviceable with Google Translate and properties prefer/offer 24/7 communication via Whatsapp.

listings.name: Caravelle Hotel
listings.content: In-house restaurants and spas. 7 km from the airport. During the war it was home to many war correspondents and the rooftop bar served as their watering hole. Today, it is also known for the afternoon tea served at its Café de l'Opera.

listings.name: Hotel Majestic
listings.content: Luxury hotel that got its start in 1925, and though it has undergone a number of renovations since, it maintains the same basic look outside. Rooftop bar serves mediocre ice cream and drinks. Has a non-smoking wing.

listings.name: JW Marriott Hotel & Suites Saigon
listings.content: Dinner buffet from USD40. Can walk to city center. Formerly Intercontinental Saigon
listings.address: Hai Bà Trưng/Góc Đ. Lê Duẩn, Bến Nghé, Quận 01

listings.name: Mövenpick Hotel Saigon
listings.content: Luxury hotel in Phu Nhuan, 10 min away from the exhibition centre and international airport and 20 min from HCMC centre. 251 rooms and suites. All rooms are equipped with individually controlled air-con, TV, minibar, safe, hairdryer. Broadband Internet in all rooms.
listings.address: 253 Nguyen Van Troi St, Phu Nhuan District

listings.name: Park Hyatt Saigon
listings.content: Luxury hotel which features a collection of contemporary Vietnamese art, a variety of non-smoking dining options including an al fresco setting, an Italian restaurant, Opera, the signature Vietnamese/Western restaurant, Square One, Park Lounge that serves afternoon tea, and a martini bar, 2 Lam Son. The hotel has a 20 m pool, fitness centre, and the Xuan Spa.

listings.name: Renaissance Riverside Hotel
listings.content: On the river and near the main tourist-shopping district, a block off of Dong Khoi.

listings.name: The Reverie Saigon
listings.content: 286 rooms and suites furnished with Italian designs, five high-end restaurants, a spa, swimming pool, fitness centre and an executive lounge.

listings.name: Saigon Domaine Luxury Residences
listings.content: Luxury serviced apartments. Cable TV, radio, air-con, safe, hair dryer, Internet, phone, mini–bar and coffee/tea maker. Swimming pool, fitness room, sauna, business facilities and currency exchange. Car rental and airport and city transfers.
listings.address: 1057 Binh Quoi Street, Ward 28, Binh Thanh District

listings.name: Sheraton Saigon
listings.content: It has a Prada shop in the arcade. Restaurants are around USD40 for an all-you-can-eat buffet dinner, wine included.

listings.name: Sherwood Residence
listings.content: Sherwood Residence is a luxury serviced apartment in HCMC. The property offers two and three bedroom apartments for short- and long-term. A private restaurant serves Western and Asian cuisine. On Pasteur Street, Sherwood Residence is within walking distance to the War Remnants' Museum and guests can take the free hourly shuttle to the business district.

listings.name: Sofitel Plaza Saigon
listings.content: 290-room hotel in the city center. Airy, if slightly small rooms, comfy beds, free wired Internet. Several restaurants, including a buffet and a breakfast spread.

listings.name: Somerset Chancellor Court Ho Chi Minh City
listings.content: The serviced residence is in the heart of the business district. It offers 172 apartments ranging from studios to three-bedroom. Each apartment is fully furnished with an open kitchen concept, contemporary Western style decor and balcony.
listings.address: 21-23 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai St, District 1

listings.name: Thao Dien Village
listings.content: A colonial-style boutique hotel in tropical gardens on the banks of the river. 22 rooms, spa and health club. 4 restaurants; Ngon (Vietnamese), Villa Romaine (Italian), Chaba (Thai), and Tama-Gawa (sushi bar). Every Saturday at 19:30 there is a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show on the riverside outdoor terrace of Ngon Restaurant.
listings.address: 195 Nguyen Van Huong St, Thao Dien Ward, District 2

listings.name: Windsor Plaza Hotel
listings.content: A high-end hotel with 386 rooms in Cholon (Ho Chi Minh City's Chinatown). Several restaurants including an extensive Western and Asian buffet on 4th floor; a Chinese restaurant serving live seafood, southern Chinese cuisine and dim sum; and a rooftop international restaurant that has panoramic views of Cholon. Guests can take the free hourly shuttle to the business district. Free Wi-Fi in public areas.

places.title: April 30 Park
places.blurb: April 30 Park is a park located in the center of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, within District 1 facing Independence Palace and behind Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon.

places.title: Chợ Lớn
places.blurb: Chợ Lớn, usually anglicized as "Cholon" in English sources, is an unofficial quarter of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Bình Tây Market
places.blurb: Bình Tây Market is the largest market in Chợ Lớn; located in Bình Tây ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Ấn Quang Pagoda
places.blurb: Ấn Quang Pagoda (Vietnamese: Chùa Ấn Quang, chữ Hán: 印光寺, meaning: "Pagoda of the Light of the Seal") in Master Vạn Hạnh Street is a meeting place for Vietnamese Buddhist leaders in Ho Chi Minh City and is a site of t…

places.title: Thống Nhất Stadium
places.blurb: Thống Nhất Stadium, formerly Cộng Hoà Stadium is the second-largest multi-purpose stadium in Ho Chi Minh City, and the oldest in Vietnam.

places.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon
places.blurb: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon, officially the Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception is a cathedral located in the Saigon ward of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Ho Chi Minh City Opera House
places.blurb: Saigon Opera House is a municipal opera house in downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Diamond Plaza
places.blurb: Diamond Plaza is a complex building in downtown Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City.

places.title: Vĩnh Nghiêm Pagoda, Ho Chi Minh City
places.blurb: Vĩnh Nghiêm Pagoda is a pagoda in an area of 6,000 square metres at 339, Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa street, Ward 7, District 3 Ho Chi Minh City.

places.title: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens
places.blurb: The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens, or locally and coloquially known as The Zoo, is Vietnam's oldest zoo and botanical garden.

places.title: Museum of Ho Chi Minh City
places.blurb: Museum of Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Gia Long Palace, is a historical site and museum in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Tân Định Church
places.blurb: Tân Định Church or Tân Định Parish Church is a Roman Catholic church in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Bến Thành Market
places.blurb: Bến Thành Market is located in the center of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam in District 1.

places.title: Saigon Bridge
places.blurb: Saigon Bridge, also known as Newport Bridge before 1975, is a bridge crossing the Saigon River, connecting Bình Thạnh District and District 2, Ho Chi Minh City now is Thủ Đức, on the Hanoi Highway.

places.title: Thủ Thiêm Bridge
places.blurb: Thủ Thiêm Bridge is a 6-lane bridge in Ho Chi Minh City, the largest city of Vietnam, opened in 2008.

places.title: Xá Lợi Pagoda
places.blurb: The Xá Lợi Pagoda is the largest pagoda in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Mariamman Temple, Ho Chi Minh City
places.blurb: The Mariamman Temple in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, is a temple dedicated to the Hindu goddess Mariamman.

places.title: Citadel of Saigon
places.blurb: The Citadel of Saigon also known as the Citadel of Gia Định was a late 18th-century fortress that stood in Saigon, Vietnam from its construction in 1790 until its destruction in February 1859.

places.title: Lê Văn Tám Park
places.blurb: Le Van Tam Park, previously known as Mạc Đĩnh Chi Cemetery, is a park in Downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Đầm Sen Park
places.blurb: Dam Sen Cultural Park is an amusement park located in Bình Thới ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Phú Mỹ Bridge
places.blurb: The Phú Mỹ Bridge is a cable-stayed road bridge over the Saigon River in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Sunwah Tower
places.blurb: Sunwah Tower or Sun Wah Tower is a high-rise Grade A office building in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
places.blurb: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts is the major art museum of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and second in the country only to the Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts in Hanoi.

places.title: Southeastern Armed Forces Museum Military Zone 7
places.blurb: The Southeastern Armed Forces Museum Military Zone 7 is a military museum located at 247 Hoàng Văn Thụ Street, Tân Sơn Hòa, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Dragon House
places.blurb: Dragon House or Dragon House Wharf, Dragon House Harbour, officially known as Ho Chi Minh Museum, Ho Chi Minh City Branch, was the original commercial port of Saigon.

places.title: Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard
places.blurb: Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard is a boulevard in District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Paris Commune Square
places.blurb: Paris Commune Square is a small square and roundabout located in Saigon ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Tao Đàn Park
places.blurb: Tao Đàn Park or fully known as Tao Đàn Cultural Park, also known as Tao Đàn Garden is an urban park in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam behind the Independence Palace with an address 55C Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Bến…

places.title: Dân Sinh Market
places.blurb: Dân Sinh Market, also known as American Market or Yersin Market, is a retail market in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City.

places.title: Hùng King Temple
places.blurb: The Hùng King Temple is a temple dedicated to the Hùng kings, the Vietnamese rulers of the Hồng Bàng dynasty.

places.title: Chi Lăng Park
places.blurb: Chi Lăng Park is a park located in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, within the jurisdiction of District 1.

places.title: Turtle Lake
places.blurb: Turtle Lake is a lake and a fountain surrounded by a traffic roundabout officially known as International Square in District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Thisofic Tower
places.blurb: Thisofic Tower or formerly Sofic Tower, initially named as Zone IIA Tower or Zone IIA HCMC, is a complex building in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Southern Women's Museum
places.blurb: The Southern Women's Museum is a history museum in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, dedicated to the contributions of women in southern Vietnam to national building, defense, and cultural preservation.

places.title: Gành Rái Bay
places.blurb: Gành Rái Bay is a large tidal estuary in Ho Chi Minh City, Southeast region of Vietnam, where the major rivers in the region meet, such as Lòng Tàu River, Đồng Tranh River, Thị Vải River and Dinh River into the low-ly…

places.title: Hòa Bình Theater
places.blurb: Hòa Bình Theater is a theater located in Hòa Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

places.title: Bến Thành Theatre
places.blurb: Bến Thành Theatre is a theatre for performing arts inside a building that technically known as District 1 Cultural Center, now is Saigon Ward Public Service Center.

places.title: Tân Định Market
places.blurb: Tân Định Market is a market in Tân Định, Central Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
